dropcap_opening_actualtext:
DEBUGGING is a central yet cognitively demanding part
of software development. Beyond locating and fixing
faults, successful debugging requires developers to interpret
symptoms, reason about possible causes, choose appropri-
ate strategies, and adapt their approach as new informa-
tion emerges [1], [2]. Developers use a range of debugging
strategies to structure this reasoning, including hypothesis
testing [3], [4], tracing dependencies and execution paths [1],
[3], [5], [6], reasoning backward from symptoms to possible
causes [3], [4], [7]–[15], and simplifying complex problem
spaces [15]–[17].
